Requirements accounted for: backend-authored opaque paths separated from labels; local and external references; stability across unrelated/detail edits, sibling movement and host reconstruction; explicit failure for rename, ownership move, deletion and forgery. The ordinary implementation association is canonical_children in sage::inspector. It constructs kind/name or anonymous identity segments with occurrence suffixes; symbol_identity_parts, stable_symbol_hash and percent_encode explain those segments. walk_symbols builds ownership paths independently of display_path/label. find_local_reference walks local ownership and validates each child; InspectorReflectionResolver supplies those references. canonical_external_reference encodes crate disambiguation and definition segments separately from label. resolve_local_symbol walks current ownership; resolve_external_path validates the root and each canonical child prefix. symbol returns symbol-not-found for missing selection; updates invalidate the directory and reconstruction clears it. These are concrete mechanisms supporting the claim, not proof of its universal stability guarantee.
The entire associated test set is one TODO function, sage_meta::todo::crates_sage_inspector_inspection_canonical_ownership. Its empty body makes no assertions and supplies no behavioral proof. Its explicit prerequisite is association and review of complete path evidence covering local association, anonymous/generated ownership, reordered siblings, rename failure, reconstruction, external parent/children and crate disambiguation, with the exact oracle suite separately accounting for navigation detail exclusion from conformance. I accept that complete-evidence deferral, including unrelated/detail stability and destructive path cases (move/deletion/forgery), rather than claiming those are covered by the placeholder or by the unrelated inline Unicode encoding test. The rationale remains sufficient as explicit unfinished test evidence; no N/A entries exist.
